title: Ask for confirmation before a bash script deletes files
summary: Deletes temporary .tmp files in one folder, but first shows the list and asks you to type yes. Anything else cancels and nothing is deleted.

warnings: Deletion is permanent. rm does not move files to the trash, so a deleted file cannot be restored by the script.
The script removes only *.tmp files directly inside the folder you name, not in its subfolders. Still, check the folder name before you type yes.
--yes skips the question. Use it only in scripts you have already tested, never for a folder you have not looked at.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# confirm-delete.sh - delete *.tmp files in one folder, but only after you confirm.
# Usage: ./confirm-delete.sh DIRECTORY [--yes]
# The script lists the files first. Then it asks you to type yes.
# --yes skips the question; use it only in scripts you have already tested.
# Deleted files are NOT moved to a trash folder: they are gone.

set -euo pipefail

if (( $# < 1 )) || [[ ! -d $1 ]]; then
    echo "usage: $0 DIRECTORY [--yes]" >&2
    exit 2
fi
DIR=$1
ASSUME_YES=0
if [[ ${2:-} == "--yes" ]]; then
    ASSUME_YES=1
fi

# Collect the list first, so the user sees exactly what will be deleted.
# mapfile -d '' (bash 4.4+) reads the NUL-separated names from find.
mapfile -d '' -t files < <(find "$DIR" -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.tmp' -print0)

if (( ${#files[@]} == 0 )); then
    echo "no *.tmp files in $DIR, nothing to do"
    exit 0
fi

echo "These ${#files[@]} file(s) will be permanently deleted:"
printf '  %s\n' "${files[@]}"

if (( ! ASSUME_YES )); then
    # read -r -p shows the question and waits for one line of typed text.
    # If there is no typed input at all (end of input), the answer stays empty.
    answer=""
    read -r -p "Type 'yes' to delete them: " answer || true
    if [[ $answer != "yes" ]]; then
        echo "cancelled, nothing was deleted"
        exit 0
    fi
fi

rm -f -- "${files[@]}"
echo "deleted ${#files[@]} file(s)"

prerequisites: A Linux terminal with bash 4 or newer

rollback.explain: The script cannot undo a deletion. If you have a backup of the folder, copy the files back from it. Otherwise the files are gone.
